Immersive and wonderful It's hard to put into words how lovely our Nile cruise on the Tui Al Horeya, was, but I'll try. We arrived at around 630/700pm on our first night after very rigorous security at Luxor Airport. Immediately our senses were blasted by the culture of Luxor. Al Horeya was berthed opposite the most beautiful stone pillars; she was it up in her splendour. Down some tricky stone steps onto her gangplank and we were gobsmacked at how elegant and swish her internals were. We went to our room where our luggage was waiting. We dined in Lazezza restaurant and already we knew we were going to have a lovely holiday. 😍 I can say, hand on heart, that I've never experienced wonderful staff like we had the pleasure of being with for 7 days. They were attentive and friendly. Every single one deserves praise but these are the ones we got closer too. Karem in the bars, Mohammed in the restaurant (I wasn't well one day and he was so caring), our cabin lad Saffy who gave us a lovely towel animal every day. Katie, our entertainment organiser, bubbly, friendly and fun, did a great job. One person who will stay in my memory is Egyptologist Ayman, boy what a warm wonderful character he is. He brought ancient Egypt to life. We were group 2 in the excursions so his catch phrase to keep us together was "Tui 2 Tui 2". There is nothing he doesn't know about ancient Egypt and his passion is in incredible. Food brilliant. Snack bar upstairs, restaurant downstairs. Tasty cocktails. The upper deck is well decked out where you get the most wonderful view of the Nile. We went to a Nubian village, loads of tombs and temples, so we certainly got our steps Being smaller than a cruise liner (around 140 people), meant we got to know each other and it was a much more intimate feeling rather than thousands of people. My favourite excursion was the sound and light show at Karnak temple. So immersive it actually made me cry but I love history so it was right up my street. There was nothing I could fault. Home time came which was well organised. We boarded the plane but after an hour the flight was abandoned due to an engine problem. Despite hundreds of people from our boat not knowing what will happen, we were taken to a very swish hotel who roomed us, gave us dinner breakfast and lunch (Tui, you were brilliant getting us sorted). All OK for the following day. Although everyone was tired (it had been a little stressful due to onward travel plans being disrupted, us having booked a ferry to our home Isle of Wight), everyone's spirits were high and very saddened to leave.All in all this holiday was wonderful (I don't like boats but I needn't have worried). Thank you Al Horeya, God bless her and all who sail in her.
